c.cr.state_control.statement: China Re is majority state-owned: Central Huijin is the controlling shareholder (71.56%) and the Ministry of Finance holds 11.45%.

c.cr.earnings_softer.statement: FY2025 earnings softened despite top-line growth: total income +5.8% but attributable net profit −7.4% and ROE down 1.56 percentage points.
c.cr.earnings_softer.caveats: Two years only; drivers of the profit decline are not decomposed here.

c.cr.underwriting_divergence.statement: Overseas P&C underwriting strengthened while domestic P&C reinsurance and primary P&C margins narrowed.
c.cr.underwriting_divergence.caveats: Segment-level ratios only; no group-level combined ratio recorded.

c.cr.capital_buffer.statement: Group solvency eased slightly in 2025 to 155% core and 189% aggregated.
c.cr.capital_buffer.caveats: 2025 solvency figures are unaudited. Regulatory minimums are not yet sourced in this record.

c.cr.ratings_stable.statement: The issuer reports its A.M. Best "A (Excellent)" and S&P "A" ratings were maintained in 2025.
c.cr.ratings_stable.caveats: Issuer-reported; agency publications, rating types, dates and outlooks not yet reviewed.

c.cr.business_mix.statement: Primary P&C insurance and P&C reinsurance are of similar size and together dominate insurance revenue; life and health reinsurance is much smaller.
c.cr.business_mix.caveats: Segment figures are before inter-segment eliminations.
